title: Object identity and mutation
learningObjectives: Explain object identity and mutation and reason about JavaScript execution and function behaviour.

understand.concept: Objects and arrays are reference values. Assigning an object to another variable copies the reference, not the object. Mutating through either reference changes the same underlying object. Shallow copying creates a new outer object but nested objects may still be shared.
understand.whyItMatters: Reference identity explains surprising state changes and is important in UI frameworks and predictable state updates. Use deliberate copying when you need an independent structure.
understand.analogy: Two variables can be two labels pointing to the same shared box; changing the box through one label is visible through the other.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript scope, execution, identity, and scheduling follow language and engine semantics.

explain.narrative: alias and original refer to the same object. The spread copy duplicates only the outer object, so the nested profile is still shared.

practise.guidedTask: Compare assignment, shallow copy, and a suitable deep-copy approach for nested plain data. Record which references remain shared.

questions.prompt: Does assigning an object to another variable create a separate independent object?
options: No, both variables refer to the same object
questions.answer: No, both variables refer to the same object
questions.explanation: Object assignment copies the reference, not the object's full contents.
